name: Pacific Rim fusion
region: Los Angeles, Honolulu and the Pacific coast
summary: French technique and Californian produce with the sauces and the fish of Asia. Chinois on Main (1983), Roy's in Honolulu (1988) and Matsuhisa and Nobu from 1987 put soy, ginger, miso and raw fish on a plated menu.

philosophy.core_thesis: A chef from one tradition can use the pantry and the flavours of another, if the cook keeps the balance of each dish and the precision of the technique.
design_principles: Cook with French method and season with the sauces of Asia: soy, ginger, miso, chilli and citrus.
Sear or wok-cook the main piece quickly and leave the centre rare.
Pair raw fish with a hot oil or a sharp dressing of yuzu and soy.
Build a sauce from a reduction of stock, a butter and an Asian seasoning, for example a soy and mustard butter sauce.
Serve a mix of small plates in the middle of the table, or an arranged plate of one main item.
Use produce of the Pacific: tuna, shellfish, tropical fruit and local greens.
Set the food on a bright plate with a clear shape, and dress it with a herb or a few strips of vegetable.
anti_patterns: A heavy cream sauce on Asian food
A dish with five unrelated spices
A tall tower with a garnish
A flat copy of one national dish

plating.composition: The main piece sits at the centre or slightly off it, with a sauce in a pool or in drops around it, and a few strips of raw vegetable or a herb on top.
plating.plate: A white or black round or square plate of 260 to 300 mm, or a shallow bowl, in a modern shape.
plating.portion: A main piece of 100 to 150 g with 40 ml of sauce; the plate is about 50 to 60 per cent full.
plating.height: The food stands 20 to 60 mm high; thin slices lie flat or lean on a small pile of vegetables.
rules: Slice raw fish thin and lay it in a single row with a little sauce over each slice.
Put a hot oil or a ponzu at the last moment, so the fish turns pale at the edge.
Set a small pile of crisp vegetable strips on top for height.
Dot or pool the sauce; do not flood the plate.
Use chopsticks and forks both on the table.

pantry.rule: Take one main ingredient from the Pacific, add one or two Asian seasonings, and finish with a French butter or a reduction.

technique.bases: A soy and ginger marinade, a miso paste, a ponzu of yuzu and soy, a chilli oil, a reduced stock and a butter sauce.
technique.details: A seared piece with a rare centre, hot oil poured on raw fish, a few strips of crisp vegetable, a sauce in dots, a thin sheet of fried noodle.

flavour.profile: Bright and salty-sweet: soy, ginger and citrus with the fat of fish or butter, and a little heat from chilli.
flavour.balance: Salt and umami from soy and miso sit against acid from yuzu or lime and sweet from tropical fruit or mirin.
flavour.fat: Butter, oil and fatty fish give about 30 to 40 per cent of the energy of a main dish.
flavour.seasoning: Soy and miso in the marinade, ginger and chilli in the sauce, citrus and fresh herbs at the last moment.

palette.strategy: Use a plain white or black plate for the pink and red of fish with the green of herbs and the amber of soy.

service.format: A lively dining room with an open kitchen and a sushi bar; the table shares small plates, then each guest has one main plate.
service.courses: Five to eight dishes: cold small plates, hot small plates, a main plate and a dessert; or a chef's omakase of eight to twelve plates.
service.tableware: White and black plates in modern shapes, chopsticks and forks, small sauce dishes and a plain table.
service.setting: A stylish restaurant with bright decoration and a kitchen of cooks trained in French and Asian method, with a chef who comes out to the table.

dishes.dish: Blackened tuna with soy and mustard butter sauce
New-style salmon sashimi with hot oil
Duck salad with ginger and soy dressing

positive: seared tuna with soy butter sauce
thin slices of raw salmon with hot oil

evidence.title: Yellowtail sashimi with jalapeño, a Nobu dish
Tuna sashimi salad with Matsuhisa dressing, a Nobu dish

emotion.target_response: The excitement of a new flavour on a familiar plate: salt, heat and citrus with the polish of a fine restaurant.

use_cases: a menu for a fusion restaurant of the 1990s
a food photograph of seared fish with an Asian sauce
a sushi bar with a French plate
avoid_when: the brief wants a pure national cuisine
the brief wants a rich classic French sauce
the brief wants only local produce of one place

modifiers.how: Cut the soy and the chilli, add olive oil and local greens, and serve on a plain plate.
Replace the butter sauce with a citrus and chilli leche, and use ceviche cuts of fish.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Pacific Rim cuisine (Cuisine of Hawaii)
